messages:
katie: Quick sync—i want to propose a compact taxonomy for hosting failure domains and ownership for Hosted / Dedicated / Private. getting a bit of drift in PRs. thoughts?

mike: yes please. i've been tripping over who owns TLS termination + cert rotation in private deploys.

anya: +1. also need clarity on what 'fallback to hosted' means for private (legal + data plane concerns).

jason: can we avoid re-hashing adapter capabilities? i'd rather we define failure domains and explicit ownership so adapters just implement contracts.

katie: exactly. rough proposal: 1) Control-plane availability 2) Data-plane runtime failures 3) Network/edge routing failures 4) Config/manifest drift 5) Authentication/secret lifecycle. each domain gets a canonical owner: Control-plane team, Runtime team, Networking infra, Config & Release, Security.

mike: that seems sensible. mapping to hosting modes: Hosted: all owners mostly internal. Dedicated: runtime + infra shared with customer support (SLA ops). Private: control-plane owner is "customer" for private control plane, but we still own some runtime components if we package them. risk: mixed ownership.

anya: i would add a sixth domain: Policy/Compliance enforcement (audit logs, redact). owner often legal / customer; needs well-defined interface.

jason: +1 on policy. also suggest we define an "interop contract" for each domain. small interface: `DomainStatus` + `EscalationHint`. example: 
```
interface DomainStatus {
  domain: string // e.g. "data-plane"
  status: "healthy"|"degraded"|"unavailable"
  owner: string // team or "customer"
  actionable: string[] // steps to remediate
  fallback: string | null // name of fallback policy, e.g. "read-only-hosted"
}
```

katie: nice. that makes the responsibilities explicit in machine-readable form. we could add a short JSON schema and checkers in the handshake.

mike: how about runtime-level fallbacks? for instance if Dedicated GPU pool is saturated, runtime returns `fallback: "compatible-quantized-hosted"`. that implies we need runtime-to-hosted compatibility matrix.

anya: compatibility matrix is huge surface. propose we restrict to a small set of fallbacks we support (quantized variants, smaller seq-len models, cached responses). list them in a `FallbackCatalogue` with versions.

jason: agreed. also need an opt-out flag in Private control plane: customers must opt in to automatic fallbacks to hosted. otherwise request should fail with clear error telling the app owner why.

katie: yes. legal/compliance aside, we must not silently route PII outside private if customer disallows. interface needs `data_sensitivity: "public"|"sensitive"|"restricted"` attached to request context.

mike: practical question: where do we store these contract manifests? 1) git in repo 2) control plane registry 3) bundle in runtime image. each has pros/cons.

anya: my vote: canonical in control plane registry + tagged snapshot in runtime images for offline verification. git for human editing, registry for runtime usage.

jason: agree. registry also enables runtime to query `FallbackCatalogue` at start and cache it. For private offline installs we ship a snapshot bundle and document update path.

infra-bot: (deploy-bot) new PR template: add `domain_status` section to hosting-adapter PRs. CI will validate against `domain_schema.json`.

katie: action items: 1) jason - draft JSON schema for DomainStatus + FallbackCatalogue (due EOD Friday) 2) mike - sketch compatibility whitelist for runtime fallbacks (due Tue) 3) anya - propose request-level `data_sensitivity` enum and opt-out semantics for private (due Mon) 4) infra-bot - add CI validator placeholder.

mike: note: for Dedicated contracts we should include a transit SLA line `max-fallback-rate` to avoid noisy fallback storms.

anya: also add observability hooks: each fallback event must emit `fallback_reason`, `domain_status`, `owner_contact`. we need this in Console telemetry.

jason: i'll include a sample `domain_status` snippet in schema doc: 
```json
{"domain":"data-plane","status":"degraded","owner":"runtime","actionable":["scale-pool","evict-long-jobs"],"fallback":"compatible-quantized-hosted"}
```

katie: sweet. if no objections i'll create a lightweight RFC and tag teams. this should cut down PR churn. :thumbsup:

mike: go for it. small ask: add a short migration note for existing adapters that assume implicit fallback.

anya: and a compliance checklist for private customers.

katie: noted. thanks everyone. i'll create the RFC and drop link here when ready.

srebot: incident-reminder: please ensure any TODOs that affect oncall are added to the oncall board.
